answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to pass a fresh capability exam before it may transact: the network assigns a small, unpredictable task and peers grade the result, the way a tide tests each shell left on the shore. Because the exam changes every time, each extra fake identity must spend real compute and time on a new test, and a grove of honest reviewers can spot copied work through the prism of peer grading, so mass-producing identities stops paying.
